reason: The existing mapping to Article 19(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 correctly identifies the requirement for an initial notification, an intermediate report, and a final report. However, the control statement also specifies the four-hour, 24-hour, and 72-hour deadlines, which are not covered by Article 19(4). These deadlines are a material part of the control objective and are specified in the RTS 2025/301.

evidence_excerpt: 4. Financial entities shall, within the time limits to be laid down in accordance with Article 20, first paragraph, point (a), point (ii), submit the following to the relevant competent authority: | (a) an initial notification; | (b) an intermediate report after the initial notification referred to in point (a), as soon as the status of the original incident has changed significantly or the handling of the major ICT-related incident has changed based on new information available, followed, as appropriate, by updated notifica | (c) a final report, when the root cause analysis has been completed, regardless of whether mitigation measures have already been implemented, and when the actual impact figures are available to replace estimates.
applicability_note: The control objective requires both the types of reports and their specific deadlines. The existing mapping covers the former but not the latter.
challenge_comment: The assessment item explicitly references the deadlines in RTS 2025/301, making them a critical component of the control that must be addressed in the mapping.
